title: General practitioners´ involvement in oncological aftercare (ACTION)
summary: The ACTION project investigates the role of general practitioners in the follow-up care of people with cancer and explores how collaboration between general practitioners and oncological specialists can be improved. The study combines analyses of health insurance and cancer registry data from Lower Saxony with surveys and interviews involving general practitioners, oncological specialists, patients, and experts. The aim is to develop practical recommendations for more coordinated and patient-centered oncological follow-up care.

interventions.name: Non-interventional observational study without intervention arms. The study comprises a linked secondary analysis of routine health insurance data from AOK Lower Saxony and data from the Clinical Cancer Registry of Lower Saxony. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
AP1a: Oncological disease (breast cancer, colorectal cancer stage II and III, melanoma), first diagnosis between 2021 and 2023, insured by AOK, residence in Lower Saxony, adult age
AP1b: Medical practice in primary care in Lower Saxony
AP1c: Medical practice in ambulatory oncological care in Lower Saxony
AP1d: Oncological disease with completed primary treatment, residence in Lower Saxony, physical and cognitive ability to participate in interviews
AP2a: Expert in oncological follow-up care in Germany, e.g. healthcare professionals from outpatient and inpatient care, representatives of professional societies and associations, patient representatives, or representatives of self-help groups
AP2b: Expert in oncological follow-up care in Germany, e.g. healthcare professionals from outpatient and inpatient care, representatives of professional societies and associations, patient representatives, or representatives of self-help groups
Exclusion criteria:
AP1a: None
AP1b: Exclusive treatment of privately insured patients, insufficient German language proficiency for study participation
AP1c: Exclusive treatment of privately insured patients, insufficient German language proficiency for study participation
AP1d: Insufficient German language proficiency for study participation
AP2a: Insufficient German language proficiency for study participation
AP2b: Insufficient German language proficiency for study participation
